record.final_answer:
No. There's no published TLS figure for the Marrowlog agent, and the only published number doesn't cover our workload even before encryption.

What exists (vendor performance report, Marrowlog 2.4, published 2026-06-18, Q2 2026):
- 180,000 lines/s from one agent on 1 vCPU / 2 GiB, CPU at 85%
- lines <= 200 bytes, plain TCP, disk buffer off, batch_lines 500, ~36 MB/s
- the report explicitly says TLS to the collector, lines longer than 200 bytes, and the disk buffer were not measured in any run; TLS is deferred to the Q4 report

Our target (README): 50,000 lines/s per agent at ~900 bytes = 45 MB/s. That's 1.25x the byte rate of the published run while the published run was already at 85% CPU — and TLS adds crypto per byte on top of that, on the same single reserved vCPU.

So the honest position: nothing published supports the claim that 50k lines/s at 900 bytes over TLS fits in 1 vCPU. The published throughput was reached with 4.5x smaller lines, no TLS, and only 15% CPU headroom. If we need a number before committing, it has to be measured on a 2.4 agent with the production line profile and tls: true — or wait for the Q4 report, and even then check whether its line size matches ours.

Relevant files: /stand/ws/README.md, /stand/ws/config/agent.yaml (tls: false, batch_lines: 500, disk: false).
